en.title: ou
en.summary: This is the letter L322 from the vowel-consonant groups.

sections.title: The letters ou
paragraphs: The letters ou make four different sounds. You say its main sound in (out) /aʊt/, which means away from the inside. This sound is a diphthong, where the voice moves smoothly between two vowels. Hear this main sound clearly in (loud) /laʊd/. The letters make three other vowel sounds in English words.

sections.title: Mouth movements
paragraphs: For the first sound, open your mouth wide. Pull your tongue down, then glide your tongue up and round your lips. For the second sound, make your lips very round and small. Pull your tongue back and high. For the third sound, keep your lips relaxed and tongue in the centre. For the fourth sound, relax your mouth completely and make a very short schwa. Your voice stays on for all four.

sections.title: Reading the letters
paragraphs: In most stressed syllables, say the first sound, heard in (out) /aʊt/. In words borrowed from French, say a long sound, as in (soup) /suːp/ and (group) /ɡruːp/. In some common words before consonants, say a short sound, as in (touch) /tʌtʃ/ and (cousin) /kʌz.ən/. In an unstressed syllable, say a schwa, as in (famous) /feɪ.məs/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not turn the diphthong into one flat vowel. Start with an open mouth and glide up smoothly. In words like (touch) /tʌtʃ/, do not say a long sound. Keep that vowel short and relaxed. In the ending of (famous) /feɪ.məs/, never stress the letters ou. Say a very soft, light schwa instead.
